title: Where in the Cancellation Window a Granite Ridge Season Pass Is Given Up
content:
How far the cancellation window has run when a Granite Ridge Season Pass Programme pass is given up raises the share at which the charge base is taken.

**First.** Where the pass is given up after two thirds of the cancellation window counted from the day the application was recorded has run, the charge base is taken at once and a half, a multiple of 1.5.

**Second.** Where the pass is given up after a third but before two thirds of that window has run, the charge base is taken at once and a quarter, a multiple of 1.25.

**Otherwise.** In any other case the charge base is not raised by this rule.

### The window divided into thirds

The window is the tier's own cancellation window, counted in days from the day the application was recorded. A Granite Ridge Summit Pass carries a window of 21 days, so a third of it is passed once 8 days have run and two thirds once 15 days have run.

| Days since the application was recorded, on a window of 21 days | Multiple taken |
| --- | --- |
| 7 | not raised by this rule |
| 8 | 1.25 |
| 14 | 1.25 |
| 15 | 1.5 |

On a Granite Ridge Collective Unlimited Pass, whose window is 30 days, a third is passed once 11 days have run and two thirds once 21 days have run.

### Worked on hypothetical figures

A Granite Ridge Summit Pass whose application was recorded on 1 November, given up on 20 November. Nineteen days have run on a window of 21, which is past two thirds of it, so the charge base is taken at a multiple of 1.5: on a charge base of 125.00 that gives 187.50.
